newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, November 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, November 26.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Majority parties expressed their support to Prime minister Romano Prodi after a magistrate recommended he should be tried for alleged abuse of office during his chairmanship of state industrial holding Iri. Prodi reacted calmly to the news, saying he has full confidence in Italy's judicial system (all).

* Political reactions were mixed in the centre-right opposition: Silvio Berlusconi said Prodi should not resign, but National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini told reporters "this affair should not be minimised" (all).
* Prosecutors in Sicily have asked justice authorities to drop a probe into Silvio Berlusconi over alleged Mafia ties on grounds of insufficient evidence (all).
* In the first day after the official re-entry into the ERM, the lira strengthened and briefly pushed through its new central parity rate of 990 lire per mark (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says the new lira parity is "sustainable" and will not penalize Italian exports as the employers association Confindustria claims. "If this was an exam, we got through with full marks," he said (Corriere, Repubblica, Stampa).
* EU Commissioner Mario Monti says the lira re-entry into Erm is positive but Italy should continue its efforts to balance public finances (Corriere).

* Metalworkers called for 10 more hours of strike after failing to find an agreement with Prodi and Confindustria over the renewal of their contract . In an interview, president of metal employers association Federmeccanica says "the new exchange rate does not favour competitiveness and will force us to be strict on (labour) costs" (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
